events.title: NHTSA closes Model S battery-fire probe (PE13-037) after underbody shield retrofit
events.summary: On March 28, 2014, NHTSA said it had closed Preliminary Evaluation PE13-037 into 15,805 2012-2013 Model S vehicles, opened after two 2013 fires in which road debris pierced the battery pack. The same day Tesla announced a triple underbody shield (a hollow aluminum bar, a titanium plate and an aluminum extrusion) fitted to cars built from March 6 and retrofitted free to existing cars. NHTSA said the shields and a November 2013 ride-height software update should reduce both underbody strikes and fire risk.

The pods held sensors and sample gear such as a satellite tracker, batteries, a desalinator and medical equipment to measure temperature, shock and vibration through launch and reentry.

events.title: Neuralink reports first speech-restoration data: 75 words a minute in week one
events.summary: On October 28, 2026, Neuralink released early data from its VOICE speech-restoration study, presented by principal investigator Dr. Nader Pouratian at the 2026 Annual NEALS Meeting. Neuralink said participants with ALS were producing text and voice at conversational rates, and that one participant reached 75 words per minute at a 5.8% word error rate on a 125,000-word vocabulary in their first week. events.title: Seoul court dismisses Tesla owners' FSD refund lawsuit
events.summary: On October 29, 2026, the Seoul Central District Court ruled against Tesla owners who had sued Tesla Korea for refunds of the Full Self-Driving option, which Tesla has sold in South Korea since March 2017. The court found the option did not promise fully driverless (Level 5) driving, that Tesla had delivered Autopilot and Enhanced Autopilot functions and, through a recent update, traffic light and sign recognition and city driving on HW3 cars, and that Tesla was not liable for delays caused by technology limits or regulation. Reuters put the plaintiffs at 88; Maeil Business Newspaper reported 89, after nine of the original filers dropped out of the suit filed in December 2024.

The public docket shows a one-page confidentiality cover letter and a placeholder for Question 8 on how Cybercab was certified to each applicable FMVSS; the substantive certification answers are not public. The only substantive public Tesla document posted with that package is the Cybercab First Responder Interaction Plan. NHTSA has not ruled on the confidentiality request and has not found Cybercab noncompliant.

events.summary: On October 30, 2026 at 9:04 p.m. PDT, SpaceX launched 27 Starlink satellites (Starlink 15-18) on a Falcon 9 from Vandenberg Space Force Base, the rocket's 700th launch. Booster B1093 landed on the droneship Of Course I Still Love You on its 18th flight, the 675th Falcon booster landing. It was SpaceX's final orbital launch of October as the company winds down Falcon 9 in favor of Starship.

events.title: UK High Court rejects X, Meta and TikTok challenge to Ofcom data demands
events.summary: On October 30, 2026, London's High Court dismissed a challenge by X, Meta and TikTok to information notices Ofcom issued in February 2026 under the Online Safety Act, which sought detailed content-moderation metrics such as posts removed or restricted and users exposed to harmful content. X had called it the most burdensome information request it had received from any regulator, costing it millions of pounds; the court rejected the argument that the requests were disproportionate. It was one of the first court tests of the UK's online safety regime.

events.title: Court denies xAI motion to dismiss NAACP Clean Air Act suit over Southaven turbines
events.summary: On October 30, 2026 Chief U.S. District Judge Debra M. Brown of the Northern District of Mississippi denied xAI's motion to dismiss the NAACP's Clean Air Act lawsuit over the gas turbines powering its Colossus 2 data center from Southaven, Mississippi. The court held that the turbines are not exempt mobile sources and need air permits, that the NAACP has standing, and that the citizen-suit provision is constitutional. The case proceeds; the court has not ruled on the NAACP's request for a preliminary injunction.

events.title: Tesla opens unsupervised Robotaxi service in Fort Worth
events.summary: On November 2, 2026 Tesla began Robotaxi rides in Fort Worth, Texas, at 6 a.m. local time with no safety monitor in the car, after its Robotaxi X account announced the start the night before. The service area covers about 143 square miles around downtown Fort Worth and launched with Model Y vehicles. Fort Worth is Tesla's seventh Robotaxi city, joining Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa.

events.title: RDW approves 'Tesla Assisted Driving' name and +10% speed cap in Europe
events.summary: The Dutch vehicle authority RDW approved changes to FSD (Supervised) in Europe, which is renamed Tesla Assisted Driving on HW4 and later cars. The maximum speed margin drops from +50% to +10% and resets to 0% at each start; Tesla delivers the changes over the air. The existing type approval stays valid, and EU-wide approval is still pending in the TCMV.

events.title: Tesla opens Berlin Engineering Center in Köpenick
events.summary: On November 4, 2026 Tesla opened the Berlin Tesla Engineering Center (BTEC) in Berlin-Köpenick, renovating an old factory complex of about 20,000 square metres between central Berlin and Giga Berlin. Tesla said the campus is its third such hub after Fremont and Shanghai, combining materials, powertrain, vehicle engineering, validation and safety testing in about 30 specialized laboratories and initially staffing about 250 engineers and technicians relocated from prior sites. The company said it is investing about €100 million and has applied for a second phase that could raise headcount to about 500.

events.title: SpaceX confirms roughly $50 billion supercompute campus plan in Cochise County, Arizona
events.summary: On November 4, 2026, SpaceX publicly confirmed it is the company behind a proposed supercompute campus in Cochise County, Arizona, near the Apache Generating Station, at a town hall covered by KVOA. The special-use application had been filed October 30, 2026, under the name Tombstone Resources L.L.C. SpaceX's November 12, 2026 official update described a roughly $50 billion campus expected to create approximately 5,500 construction jobs and 1,000 permanent jobs, using dry cooling with no planned industrial groundwater consumption; a Cochise County Planning and Zoning Commission hearing is set for December 9, 2026.

events.title: Google executive Donald Harrison resigns from SpaceX board
events.summary: Donald Harrison, Google's president of Global Partnerships and Corporate Development, notified SpaceX on November 4, 2026 that he was resigning from its board, effective immediately, after more than a decade as a director. SpaceX disclosed the resignation on November 6 and said it was not due to any disagreement over its operations, policies or practices. Alphabet is SpaceX's largest single institutional holder, with about 555 million shares.

events.title: SpaceX selects Qualcomm for Starlink Mobile nationwide terrestrial 5G
events.summary: On November 4, 2026 Qualcomm announced a multi-year agreement to supply Dragonwing radio equipment, baseband units and software for SpaceX's Starlink Mobile planned nationwide terrestrial 5G network. The equipment is to be deployed across tens of thousands of U.S. macro cell sites starting in 2027, combining terrestrial 5G with Starlink satellite connectivity as SpaceX seeks to become a major U.S. wireless carrier. Qualcomm called it its biggest 5G deal yet and did not disclose financial terms.

events.title: Musk: Cybertruck production at Giga Texas winds down mid-2027 for Cybercab
events.summary: On the evening of November 5, 2026 PT (06:30 UTC November 6), Elon Musk posted on X that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production. Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill wrote that Cybertruck was a technology development platform that lives on through Cybercab; Musk later replied that the Cybertruck fleet will be around for a long time. Tesla did not say whether Cybertruck would move to another factory.

events.title: FAA proposes streamlined commercial launch and re-entry rules
events.summary: On November 5, 2026 the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration proposed streamlining its rules for commercial space launches and re-entries, including clearer thresholds for when a flight abort is mandatory and revised rules for vehicle breakup and falling-debris risk to people on the ground. The FAA said it plans to overhaul its space licensing framework next year and is expanding its Office of Commercial Space Transportation with a team of aerospace engineers to speed approvals. Reuters reported the changes would make launch approvals easier for SpaceX and Blue Origin; the White House goal is at least 1,000 launches and re-entries a year by 2030.

events.title: Tesla opens Robotaxi service in San Antonio
events.summary: On November 9, 2026 Tesla began Robotaxi rides in San Antonio, Texas, at 5 a.m. local time, after its Robotaxi X account announced the start just after midnight with a map of the launch geofence. The posted zone runs from Loop 1604 on the north side to just south of downtown, about 274 square miles by Robotaxi Tracker's measurement, though the airport inside it is not served. San Antonio is Tesla's eighth Robotaxi city; Tesla gave no fleet size, hours or safety-monitor details.

events.title: SpaceX seeks tax abatement for $24 billion Starbase gas plant and supercompute site
events.summary: A public hearing notice reported by Reuters on November 9, 2026 shows SpaceX plans a roughly $24 billion gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility at Starbase, Texas, and has applied for a property tax abatement. The Starbase City Commission will consider the abatement and an economic development agreement on December 9, 2026. In a November 12, 2026 official update, SpaceX said the project has already generated more than 3,000 construction jobs and is expected to support more than 500 permanent jobs once operational, will generate its own electricity without drawing power from the public grid, and has committed $220 million to expand Brownsville water and wastewater infrastructure, of which it said it has already provided $40 million to the Brownsville Public Utilities Board.

events.title: Site work begins at Tesla's $10.1 billion Project Crystal Sun solar factory site near Houston
events.summary: Drone footage recorded November 8 and posted November 9, 2026 showed clearing, grading and equipment staging on Tesla's roughly 3,000-acre Project Crystal Sun site in Fort Bend County, Texas, and Musk replied "Project Crystal Sun" on X the same day. Tesla's state incentive filings describe a $10.1 billion vertically integrated plant making silicon ingots, wafers, cells and solar modules, with construction in 2026 to 2028 and commercial operations targeted for the first quarter of 2029. Fort Bend County approved incentive agreements for the project in October 2026.

events.title: Boring Company starts digging Morgan's Inclusion Tunnel in San Antonio
events.summary: On November 10, 2026 The Boring Company began tunneling on Morgan's Inclusion Tunnel, a nearly mile-long accessible underground link on the Morgan's Inclusion Campus in San Antonio, which serves people with disabilities. The route connects Morgan's Hotel and Morgan's Wonderland with stops at Morgan's Wonder Care and the Multi-Assistance Center; the Prufrock-5 machine arrived on site October 14. An anonymous private donor is funding the project, and no opening date was given.

events.title: Neuralink registers PRIME2 study adding chronic ischemic stroke
events.summary: Neuralink's PRIME2 early feasibility study (NCT07929792) was first posted on ClinicalTrials.gov on November 10, 2026 and is listed as recruiting. It plans to enroll about 10 adults with spinal cord injury, ALS or chronic ischemic stroke, who will use the N1 implant, placed by the R1 robot, to control a cursor or virtual keyboard. It is the first Neuralink study to include stroke patients.

events.title: SEC finishes paying out the 2018 "funding secured" Fair Fund
events.summary: On November 10, 2026 the SEC told a Manhattan federal court it had finished distributing the $40 million Fair Fund built from the $20 million fines Musk and Tesla each paid to settle the 2018 "funding secured" case, and asked the judge to close it. A claims administrator paid $41.53 million, with interest and after fees, to 3,350 eligible claimants, covering 51.7% of their approved losses; 3,046 claims were rejected. About $449,000 left over goes to the US Treasury.

events.title: Starlink introduces Mini 2 portable dish
events.summary: On November 10, 2026 at 9:28 AM PT, @Starlink introduced Mini 2, the next-generation portable Starlink, and opened preorders. It runs up to 4.5 hours on a quick-swap battery or on USB-C power, has built-in Wi-Fi, and Starlink says it connects in 60 seconds. On November 23, @Starlink said US preorders are open by invitation.

events.title: Tesla Robotaxi begins running 24/7 in every city it serves
events.summary: On the evening of November 11, 2026 Tesla's official Robotaxi account posted that the service now runs 24/7 in every city where it is available, ending the overnight shutdown. That covers its eight unsupervised markets: Austin, Dallas, Fort Worth, Houston and San Antonio in Texas, and Miami, Orlando and Tampa in Florida. Hours had grown in steps from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. in August to 6 a.m. to 2 a.m. in late October, and Tesla had said on its October earnings call it would unlock 24/7 operation before the end of 2026.

events.title: Tesla confirms Chicago's first 50 Semis on the way to HMD Trucking
events.summary: On November 11, 2026, Tesla's official Semi account said Chicago's first 50 Semis were on their way to the city. The only 50-truck Chicago order belongs to HMD Trucking, which took its first truck on November 2 as the first Tesla Semi registered in Illinois; the deal is worth about $15 million. Tesla does not report Semi deliveries in its quarterly numbers, so this is one of few public delivery data points since Nevada volume production began.

events.title: Finland approves Tesla Assisted Driving
events.summary: On November 11, 2026 Finland's transport agency Traficom said Tesla's Assisted Driving system, the supervised FSD renamed for Europe, is permitted on Finnish roads. Traficom recognized the Dutch RDW's provisional type approval, so Tesla can offer it to Finnish customers at once. Finland joins the Netherlands, Estonia, Croatia and Belgium ahead of a still-pending EU-wide decision.

events.title: xAI launches Grok Bot 1.0
events.summary: On November 11, 2026 xAI (SpaceXSI) launched Grok Bot 1.0, the first full release of its AI teammate agents after the August beta. It adds shared Team Bots that work in Slack, Microsoft Teams and video calls, bots that offer to take on work unprompted, and faster browser use, documents and presentations. Team Bots come on Team and Enterprise plans.

events.title: Tesla opens invite-only Cybercab orders for personal use at $29,990
events.summary: On November 13, 2026 Tesla posted on X that select customers are being invited to buy a Cybercab for personal use, priced at $29,990 plus a required $299-a-month Autonomy Subscription, with an estimated delivery of December 2026. Buyers must take delivery in Texas, and the car runs unsupervised only inside Tesla's Robotaxi service areas; the order agreement bars resale without Tesla's permission and lets Tesla repurchase the vehicle. Musk said the fee is too high and should be closer to about $115 a month, and that availability will widen as regulators approve.

events.title: Starship Flight 15: first upper-stage tower catch; booster lost offshore
events.summary: Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase Pad 2 at 4:47 p.m. CT on November 13, 2026, reached orbit and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. After 14 orbits and about 22.5 hours, Ship 42 returned to Starbase on November 14 and was caught by the tower arms, the first catch of a Starship upper stage. Super Heavy Booster 22 ended its boostback burn early on a low fuel mass alarm, aborted its catch, diverted to the Gulf and was destroyed by its flight termination system after the landing burn.

events.title: About 5,000 gallons of heat-transfer fluid spill at xAI's Southaven data center site
events.summary: On November 14, 2026 about 5,000 gallons of DOWFROST HD, a propylene glycol-based heat-transfer fluid, spilled at xAI's facility in Southaven, Mississippi, and some reached a drainage ditch. SpaceX said a contractor had attached a misconfigured hose to a mobile tank; the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality estimated 5,000 to 6,000 gallons. MDEQ said the fluid did not reach Horn Lake Creek, posed no immediate threat to public health and is overseeing cleanup.

events.title: Texas issues air permit for SpaceX's Starbase gas plant and supercompute site
events.summary: On November 16, 2026 the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality issued an air permit for SpaceX's planned $24 billion supercompute site and gas-fired power plant near Starbase. The permit covers 35 natural-gas turbines totaling about 750 MW. TCEQ said it had resumed permitting of supercomputing facilities after Governor Greg Abbott ordered a pause in September; the permit came three days after environmental groups filed a complaint alleging construction had begun without one.

events.title: Tesla plans €3 billion Giga Berlin expansion to build up to 1 million Cybercabs a year
events.summary: On November 16, 2026 Tesla said in a statement to Reuters that it will invest €3 billion (about $3.3 billion) in an additional production facility at its Grünheide plant near Berlin, aimed at producing up to 1 million Cybercabs. Tesla said it will file a building permit application for the project before the end of 2026, start construction in the first half of 2027 and begin production in 2029. Several hundred new workers are to be hired for the first phase of construction and production planning.

events.title: X suspends AI training on Grok Bot third-party data at Irish regulator's request
events.summary: On November 16, 2026 Ireland's Data Protection Commission said X had confirmed it suspended using third-party personal data collected by its Grok Bot agent to train AI models. X had begun that processing in late October 2026; the DPC had raised significant concerns and asked for the suspension. The DPC said it would engage further with X on what happened and next steps.

events.title: Tesla Energy unveils Powercore, a solid-state medium-voltage transformer
events.summary: Tesla introduced Powercore on November 17, 2026 through its Tesla Megapack account on X: a single solid-state unit that combines a medium-voltage transformer, inverter and breaker, rated 7.4 MW (9 MVA) continuously at 34.5 kV AC with 10 MVA of grid-forming peak power. Tesla's spec sheet lists 800 to 2,000 V DC input, 98.86% peak efficiency and up to a 25-year warranty, and pitches it for Megablock storage, utility solar and 800 V DC data centers, where Tesla says it is working with Nvidia. It is made in the US, with first units operating in 2027; Tesla named no price, customer or factory.

events.title: Tesla opens first Semi Megacharger in Texas, at Mesquite
events.summary: On November 17, 2026 Tesla Charging listed a new 8-stall Tesla Megacharger in Mesquite, Texas, on the east side of Dallas, and the Tesla Semi account called it the first Megacharger in Texas, saying Tesla is scaling Semi charging and service in the state. Electrek counted 7 public Megacharger sites and 44 stalls on Tesla's map after the opening, against the 37 sites Tesla had planned to open in 2026.

events.title: Musk says Starlink direct-to-cell V2 launches start in 2027, plus rooftop microcells
events.summary: At the DealBook Summit on November 18, 2026, Musk said SpaceX will start launching its second-generation direct-to-cell Starlink constellation next year, with roughly 40 times the bandwidth of the current satellites. He said SpaceX has designed small rooftop stations using its 800 MHz spectrum to carry Starlink Mobile indoors, possibly bundled with Starlink terminals, and that he thinks production starts next year. He gave no service launch date.

events.title: Musk says Tesla plans a driverless Model Y with no steering wheel or pedals
events.summary: Speaking at The New York Times DealBook Summit on November 18, 2026, Elon Musk said Tesla plans an autonomous version of the Model Y without a steering wheel or pedals, meant to carry groups of six or seven people alongside the two-seat Cybercab. He gave no launch date, price or factory, and did not say whether it would be sold to customers or kept for the Robotaxi fleet. He also called the Model Y L Tesla's most popular car and suggested all Model Y production might move to the longer version.

events.title: Tesla files for a $3.1 billion solar polysilicon refinery in Nueces County, Texas
events.summary: A Texas JETI tax-incentive application posted November 18, 2026 shows Tesla proposing a $3.1 billion refinery near Robstown in Nueces County that would turn trichlorosilane into solar-grade polysilicon for high-efficiency solar cells. The filing targets construction from 2027, commercial operations in 2030, and 515 direct jobs by 2032. It would supply the raw material upstream of Tesla's Project Crystal Sun cell and panel factory.

events.title: Boring Company signs 40-year Nashville airport station deal
events.summary: On November 19, 2026 The Boring Company said it had signed a 40-year agreement with the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority for a Music City Loop station at Nashville International Airport. The company says the station will sit 22 feet from the terminal entrance, with rides to downtown in under 10 minutes. The airport board had reviewed the license terms in February, with Boring paying to build, operate and maintain the system.

events.title: Tesla opens public Cybercab rides in Dallas
events.summary: On November 19, 2026, @robotaxi posted "Howdy Dallas. Cybercab has arrived in your city," opening public Cybercab rides in Dallas through the Tesla Robotaxi app. Dallas is the second city after Austin to get the two-seat Cybercab with no steering wheel or pedals. Tesla's Robotaxi service in Dallas has run Model Y vehicles unsupervised since April 18, 2026. This delivers the November Dallas launch stated on the October 21 earnings call.

events.title: Supercharger Waitlist goes live at 300 US sites
events.summary: On November 19, 2026 Tesla Charging said its Supercharger Waitlist was live at 300 US Supercharger sites. Drivers join a virtual queue in the Tesla app or on the car's touchscreen, and non-Tesla EV drivers can join through the app. The feature grew from a five-site pilot in California and New York that began in May 2026.

events.title: Italy approves Tesla Assisted Driving
events.summary: On November 20, 2026 Italy's Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport granted provisional type approval to Tesla Assisted Driving, the supervised FSD renamed for Europe, after a technical feasibility check. Transport Minister Matteo Salvini announced it on X, and Tesla Europe posted "Now approved in Italy, rollout begins soon" without a date. Italy is the 12th EU country to allow the system and the first of the bloc's large markets; an EU-wide vote is not expected before December.

events.title: UK High Court enters judgment for X against two Creator Revenue Sharing defendants
events.summary: The High Court in London entered judgment against two defendants that X sued in September 2026, alleging a network of accounts manipulated engagement to draw Creator Revenue Sharing payouts. X general counsel James Burnham announced it on November 24, 2026 with the first page of the order. X alleged the network collected more than £207,000; the terms of the judgment are not public.

events.title: Tesla begins rolling out FSD v15
events.summary: On November 21, 2026 at 11:24 AM PT, @Tesla posted that FSD v15 was starting to roll out, upgrading every part of the end-to-end driving network. Tesla cited 25x better handling of safety-critical cases, a new Tesla Reality View that visualizes what FSD is planning, and navigation at the start and end of a drive, with later v15 releases to expand that to the entire route. @aelluswamy said it was releasing to the first wave of customers that day. The same afternoon, @TeslaSI posted release notes that include an upgraded vision encoder shared between FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus. On November 20, Elon Musk said FSD V15 goes to wide release next month.

events.title: SpaceX forgoes BEAD subsidies under new NTIA model agreement
events.summary: On November 23, 2026, NTIA announced a BEAD model agreement for low-Earth-orbit providers that keep their awarded locations but decline the subsidy, and SpaceX agreed to serve its Starlink locations under it. SpaceX must still deliver 100/20 Mbps, pass BEAD performance testing, give new subscribers equipment at no cost, offer a low-cost plan and report every six months. States can sign the model agreement or rebid the locations.

events.title: Tesla files with German cartel office to buy assets of machine-tool maker EMAG
events.summary: On November 23, 2026 Tesla notified Germany's Federal Cartel Office (Bundeskartellamt) of an asset acquisition from the EMAG Group, a machine-tool maker based in Salach near Stuttgart; the office published the filing on November 27 as case B5-132/26. The notice covers manufacturing systems and machines for precision and electrochemical machining of metal parts and laser processing. Tesla had earlier set up a renamed company, Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE, at EMAG's headquarters; no price or scope has been disclosed.

events.title: Neuralink receives FDA approval to launch LINK pivotal study
events.summary: Neuralink announced on November 25, 2026 that the FDA approved the LINK Pivotal Study, the first pivotal trial of an implantable brain-computer interface in the US. It will test the safety and effectiveness of the N1 system in adults with severe paralysis from ALS. Neuralink says it has 30+ implanted participants across early feasibility studies in the US, Canada and the UK. The approval is to run the trial; the implant is not approved for commercial use.

events.title: Tesla nearly doubles its Dallas Robotaxi service area and cuts fares
events.summary: On November 25, 2026 Tesla's Robotaxi account posted a larger Dallas service-area map with the words "Just grew wider in Dallas. More cars, less $." Third-party measurements put the zone at about 150 square miles, up from about 82, with most new coverage north past I-635 toward Farmers Branch, Addison, Carrollton and Richardson. Tesla did not say how many cars it added or how much fares fell.

events.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX's Starmind constellation of up to 1 million orbital data-center satellites
events.summary: On November 25, 2026 the FCC Space Bureau granted in part SpaceX's January 2026 application for the SpaceX Orbital Data Center System (Starmind), a constellation of up to 1,000,000 satellites meant to operate as data centers in orbit at roughly 500 to 1,002 km (order DA 26-1273). The grant covers backup and emergency telemetry, tracking and command in Ka-band frequencies on a non-interference basis, and requires the first satellite to be operating by November 25, 2033, 10% of the constellation by 2035, 50% by 2038 and the full system by 2040. The FCC deferred SpaceX's request to dispose of satellites above 600 km without atmospheric re-entry; SpaceX must seek a modification before deploying any such satellites.

events.title: SpaceX commits one new share to every active Trump Account; Musk to match
events.summary: On November 25, 2026 SpaceX announced it will contribute one newly issued share of Class A common stock to every currently active Trump Account, the tax-advantaged investment accounts for American children. Elon Musk will personally match the number of shares SpaceX contributes, so each account would get two shares, and President and COO Gwynne Shotwell separately announced a personal gift of over 2 million SpaceX shares. SpaceX's release says the contributions are subject to risks including third-party and government approvals.
